unit.title: Probability & conjecture
unit.subtitle: Guessing with the future and conditional — no “quizás” required

grammar.title: Guess like a native — without saying “maybe”
grammar.intro: Spanish makes an elegant move English can't: it uses the future tense to guess about the present and the conditional to guess about the past. «Serán las tres» doesn't mean “they will be three” — it means “it must be about three.” Add deber de + infinitive for suppositions and you can express probability without a single “quizás”.

sections.heading: Future = a guess about NOW
sections.body: The simple future can express a guess about the present — “must be / probably is”:

ex.en: It must be about three o'clock.
ex.note: not a prediction — a guess about now

sections.heading: Conditional = a guess about the PAST
sections.body: The conditional expresses a guess about a past situation — “must have been / probably was”:

ex.en: It must have been about three when he arrived.

sections.heading: Future perfect = a guess about the recent past
sections.body: Use the future perfect (habré/habrá + participle) to guess about something that has just happened:

ex.note: guess about a completed recent action

ex.en: She's not answering; she's probably fallen asleep.
ex.note: se habrá dormido = 'she must have fallen asleep'

sections.heading: deber de + inf, and a lo mejor vs quizá
sections.body: Deber de + infinitive = supposition (must be). Careful: deber + infinitive (no de) = obligation. A lo mejor takes the indicative; quizá(s) / tal vez usually take the subjunctive:
conj: Debe de estar cansado (he must be tired)
Debe estar aquí a las ocho (he must be here at 8)

takeaways: Future of probability = guess about NOW: Serán las tres = It must be about three.
Conditional of probability = guess about the PAST: Serían las tres cuando llegó.
Future perfect = guess about the recent past: Habrá salido = He must have left.
deber de + inf = supposition; deber + inf = obligation. a lo mejor + indicative; quizá(s) + subjunctive.

mistakes.w: Debe de venir a las ocho en punto (it's his duty).
mistakes.r: Debe venir a las ocho en punto.
mistakes.why: For obligation use deber + infinitive; deber de is only for supposition.
A lo mejor takes the indicative (viene), not the subjunctive.

mistakes.w: Son las tres, supongo. (as a guess about now, plainly)
mistakes.why: To guess about the present, Spanish naturally uses the future: serán.

exercises.prompt: No sé la hora exacta. ___ las tres (guess about now).
exercises.prompt_en: I don't know the exact time. It must be about three.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! futuro de probabilidad: serán = must be now.
exercises.no: A guess about now uses the future: “Serán las tres”.

exercises.prompt: ___ las tres cuando llegó (guess about the past).
exercises.prompt_en: It must have been about three when he arrived.
exercises.no: A guess about the past uses the conditional: “Serían las tres cuando llegó”.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! futuro perfecto de probabilidad: habrá salido.
exercises.no: “Habrá salido ya” — the future perfect guesses about the recent past.

exercises.prompt: Trabaja doce horas al día. Debe ___ estar agotado.
exercises.prompt_en: He works twelve hours a day. He must be exhausted.
exercises.hint: Supposition (not obligation) needs deber + this little word + infinitive.
exercises.no: Supposition uses “deber de estar”: he must be exhausted.

exercises.prompt: Match each Spanish guess to its English meaning.

exercises.translation: She's not answering; she's probably fallen asleep.
exercises.no: It was: “No contesta; se habrá dormido.” (She must have fallen asleep.)

exercises.scenario: Wondering why a friend hasn't shown up ⏰

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.es: Ya son las nueve y Ana no llega. ¿Qué le habrá pasado?
lines.en: It's already nine and Ana isn't here. What could have happened to her?

options.text: Se habrá quedado en el trabajo.
Se ha quedar en el trabajo.
Quizá se queda en el trabajo, seguro.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! futuro perfecto = conjetura sobre el pasado reciente.
exercises.no: To guess about what just happened, use the future perfect: “Se habrá quedado en el trabajo”.

exercises.say: Debe de estar cansado; serán ya las diez
exercises.en: He must be tired; it must be about ten already
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “debe de estar… serán ya”.

vocab.en: it must be (a guess about now)
